zakatClaimEvidence: The Islamic Society of Northwest Suburbs of Chicago (ISNS) explicitly accepts zakat donations, providing a dedicated 'Zakat' section on its website. It states, "Donate your ZAKAT to ISNS. Donate your Zakat online and ISNS shall distribute it to the needy Muslims in our local community." The organization also outlines methods for submitting zakat applications and donations, including online forms, email, in-person drop-offs, and mail to their Zakah Committee. (Source: https://isns.org/services/community-services/zakat/)

strengths_deep_dive: The Islamic Society of Northwest Suburbs of Chicago demonstrates operational efficiency through its high program ratio. Financial filings show a <cite id="3">Program expense ratio of 92.1%</cite> in FY2024, beating the 75% industry standard and exceeding the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 88.7%</cite>. Furthermore, Charity Navigator reports <cite id="1">fundraising costs of <$0.01 per $1 raised</cite>, ensuring public contributions go directly toward religious programs and school management.
rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Society of Northwest Suburbs of Chicago operates a community mosque and educational center, serving the local Muslim population since its founding in 1974. In FY2024, the organization reported <cite id="3">Total Revenue of $3,697,122</cite>, down 10% from $4,092,615 in FY2023. Operational spending remains centered on its core mission, including daily prayers, weekend and preschool academics at Al-Safa Academy, and local relief operations. The charity maintains a <cite id="1">3-star rating of 77/100 from Charity Navigator</cite>, backed by strong program spending allocation. Financial filings indicate a <cite id="3">Program expense ratio of 92.1%</cite> in FY2024, which meets the benchmark ratio for programmatic output. However, financial health metrics reflect <cite id="1">117.3 months of working capital reserves</cite>. For a ZAKAT-ELIGIBLE institution, accumulating over nine years of operational reserves presents a significant structural consideration, as zakat collections are meant to reach qualifying recipients promptly rather than build long-term capital balances.
